messages:
Samir: quick sync on analytics ingestion path. svc-analytics (private subnet) needs to call partner API over TLS. three quick asks: 1) Is outbound TCP/443 to partner CIDR 203.0.113.0/24 allowed from our private subnets? 2) We need an IAM role for svc-analytics to read logs in redwood-logs (only a specific prefix). any objections to scoped read-only? 3) Flow logs / logging: will delivered logs include query params or full request URLs? security needs redaction guidance. pinging @Lisa and infra for signoff.

Lisa: TL;DR: outbound ok with contract + allowlist. Prefer Interface VPCE if partner can peer or provide a VPCE endpoint; if not, NAT gateway is acceptable with tight egress controls. FWIW VPC Flow Logs capture IP/port/protocol only — they do NOT include HTTP paths or query params. App or ALB access logs may include URLs; those must be handled separately. Please open a Jira with a redaction plan + owner.

Alex: partner confirmed they don't offer a VPCE. NAT is the only option. Plan: put the analytics subnet (10.10.3.0/24) behind nat-analytics and restrict SG egress to partner CIDR on 443. Example iptables for host-level enforcement:
```
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 203.0.113.0/24 --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP  # default deny for other destinations
```
Or security group egress rule: Allow TCP 443 -> 203.0.113.0/24 only.

Maria: for the svc account, don't attach broad AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess. Create a role with a scoped policy such as:
```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-logs/logs/analytics/*"]}]}
```
Also add a bucket policy that limits GetObject to the role's arn and conditionally requires aws:sourceVpc or aws:sourceVpce if we later use a VPCE. Recommend SSE-KMS (customer-managed key) and kms:ViaService conditions.

Lisa: agree on least privilege. Additional requirements: use SSE-KMS with a CMK (document alias/arn in the ticket), require redaction of any PII (query params, tokens) before long-term retention. If redaction can't be done inline, put raw logs into a short-term quarantine bucket with 90d retention and move redacted output to the retention bucket. Need an audit trail for redaction. Ticket must name owners and the redaction mechanism (Lambda/processor) + perf/cost estimates.

Samir: sounds good. I'll open Jira REDACT-789 and propose owners: Alex for network changes (SG + route table + change-id) and Maria for IAM + redaction prototype. Proposed change window: Tue 02:00 UTC next week. Flag if that collides with any infra freeze.

Alex: ack, I can own the infra work. I'll add a tiny terraform snippet in the PR and include the change-id. Terraform egress rule example:
```hcl
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "analytics_to_partner" {
  type        = "egress"
  from_port   = 443
  to_port     = 443
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["203.0.113.0/24"]
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.analytics_sg.id
}
```
Also will add route table entry: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-analytics for the analytics subnet only. I'll include change window and contact info in the PR.

InfraBot: deploy-plan: change request queued. Please include jira-id (REDACT-789) and the change window in the PR. Automated checks will run once PR includes terraform and iam policy.

Maria: I'll prototype a Lambda transform that strips query params and masks bearer tokens before writing to the retention bucket. Will run it in staging against sample traffic and report perf/cost. Created REDACT-789 and linked sample Lambda POC.

Lisa: Approved pending Jira REDACT-789 containing: scoped IAM policy, bucket CMK details, redaction design + owner, and the infra PR with the SG egress + route changes. :white_check_mark: Ensure audit logging for the redaction processor (CloudTrail events and object metadata flags).

Samir: great, thanks all. I'll attach security sign-off to REDACT-789 and schedule the change window. tagging owners: @Alex @Maria. Will update here if anything changes :thumbsup:
